query: How should a RAG system be evaluated in production?
report:
## Summary

A RAG system should be scored on context precision and context recall separately, because one number hides which half of the pipeline broke [1].

## Worked example

When a retriever returns twelve passages and only three of them contain the answer, context precision is three out of twelve while context recall may still be high [2]. The TREC track measures both quantities separately [2].

citations.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
citations.content: Combining parametric memory with non-parametric memory through retrieval has become a common approach to knowledge-intensive tasks. Evaluation of retrieval-augmented generation pipelines remains fragmented, with published systems reporting metrics that are rarely comparable across papers. Context precision measures whether the retrieved passages that are ranked highly are actually relevant to the question being asked.
citations.snippet: Combining parametric memory with non-parametric memory through retrieval has become a common approach to knowledge-intensive tasks.

citations.title: TREC Retrieval-Augmented Generation Track Overview
citations.content: The TREC Retrieval-Augmented Generation track measures context precision and context recall separately. Context recall asks what fraction of the relevant information required to answer the question was actually retrieved by the system. Context precision asks what fraction of the retrieved information was actually relevant. When a retriever returns twelve passages and only three of them contain the answer, context precision is three out of twelve while context recall may still be high.
citations.snippet: The TREC Retrieval-Augmented Generation track measures context precision and context recall separately.
